answer: In a PoA attestation graph, trust propagates through a bounded-length random walk whose transition kernel limits mass leakage. An honest-to-sybil bridge is scarce when the adversarial cluster has a sparse external cut; its low conductance traps walk probability internally. Spectral expansion and min-cut transitivity bounds therefore cap the cluster’s aggregate voting weight, preventing sybils from amplifying influence while preserving the nectar of honest attestations.
